NVDA.text: Nvidia rose about 3.0% as strong CoreWeave and other AI-infrastructure results revived the AI hardware trade, while in-line CPI reduced rate-hike fears and lifted the Nasdaq.

AVGO.text: Broadcom finished essentially flat despite a 0.5% Nasdaq gain; no fresh company-specific catalyst was confirmed, leaving it a notable laggard during Wednesday's AI-infrastructure rally.

TSM.text: TSM gained about 1.7% with the AI and chip rally as strong infrastructure earnings reinforced advanced-compute demand, while in-line CPI eased rate concerns.

ASML.text: ASML added about 0.6% as semiconductor and AI-infrastructure shares strengthened after upbeat technology earnings and an in-line CPI report; no distinct ASML-specific catalyst was confirmed.

KLAC.text: KLA jumped about 3.9% as the AI-infrastructure rally broadened into chips and semiconductor equipment after strong CoreWeave and other technology results boosted confidence in continued data-center spending.

INTC.text: Intel rose about 3.3% as AI-infrastructure stocks rallied on strong technology earnings, extending its rebound after investors absorbed this week's large equity offering.

MU.text: Micron jumped about 4.9% as strong CoreWeave and other AI-infrastructure earnings lifted demand expectations across the AI hardware chain, making memory a major beneficiary of Wednesday's rally.

DDOG.text: Datadog fell about 2.4% despite a rising Nasdaq; no fresh catalyst was confirmed, and the stock remained under pressure from last week's earnings reaction and concerns about modest sequential growth.

META.text: Meta fell about 3.4% even as the Nasdaq rose 0.5%; no fresh market-moving company catalyst was confirmed, so the move appears primarily stock-specific rather than a broad technology selloff.

PLTR.text: Palantir fell about 2.2% despite a stronger Nasdaq, with no fresh company-specific catalyst confirmed after its recent earnings-driven surge; the session looked like a pullback after that run.

SPCX.text: SpaceX surged about 9.6% after Elon Musk's all-hands highlighted 22 million Starlink mobile subscribers, satellite-to-cell growth and ambitious AI-compute plans, while lockup anxiety continued to ease.
